correction_record.cap_note: Q2's UPPER side uses the FULL n_a/n_b. Recomputing the 16r upper side from the full-n columns gives 342/990 with median 0.591263, matching the artifact's self-reported values digit for digit. The 20,000-flow per-service cap on lower_n_a/lower_n_b applies ONLY to the LOWER side eps_lo (fed to the Michel lower bound). Therefore 342/990 is on the SAME n calibre as Q1's 340/990 and the two may be placed side by side.
correction_record.coefficient_correction: The coefficient 31 was exactly 2x too large; 16 is the sum-to-zero-constrained value because sum(delta)=0 makes positive and negative mass equal, so L1 <= m*r and TV <= (m/2)*r, giving 16r at m=32.
correction_record.weissman_limitation: The Weissman categorical form 0.5*(sqrt(m)+c)/sqrt(n) (~935/990) is UNPROVEN for this estimator and MUST NOT be quoted: it is a bound for IID one-hot categorical observations, whereas this estimator is the mean of correlated simplex vectors; Var(f_i(c)) <= P(c)(1-P(c)) holds but per-coordinate variance bounds do NOT establish an L1 concentration inequality for correlated coordinates.
correction_record.population_note: The only genuine calibre difference is WHICH FLOW POPULATION each object admits. Q2 takes any flow with a PHIST record; Q1 requires PPI_LEN >= 5 for k=5 eligibility. The measured per-service n differs by a median of 0.5%, which does not change the conclusion.
correction_record.reproduction_note: The 342 figure has been reproduced by two independent recomputations and no longer rests on a single source.

m041_cross_check_2x2.recomputed_by: Director, independently of the agent's hand transcription, on the same 990 joined pairs
m041_cross_check_2x2.diagonal: 340 vs 342 — diagonal only; carries no corroborative weight (see off_diagonal_spread 81-935)
m041_cross_check_2x2.root_cause: The underlying statistics differ by about 2.7x (tv_hat median 0.5805 for Q1 vs 0.2157 for Q2) while the radius constants differ by about 7.34x. Two large differences in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS cancel to the same fraction.
m041_cross_check_2x2.verdict: 340 vs 342 is NOT a cross-check. A numerical coincidence produced by opposite-direction cancellation carries no corroborative weight.
m041_cross_check_2x2.rule: To call an agreement a cross-check, compute this 2x2 FIRST. Agreement that holds only where each side uses its OWN convention is CANCELLATION, not CONFIRMATION.
m041_cross_check_2x2.note_on_the_935_cell: The (Q2 tv_hat, c_Q1) cell is NOT a third symmetric convention, and must not be presented as a legitimate counterfactual. Applying Q1's constant to Q2 IS IDENTICALLY applying the Weissman categorical form: 0.5*(sqrt(32) + sqrt(2 ln(2/0.025))) = 4.30863 is the same number. That bound was already refused as UNPROVEN for Q2's estimator (it assumes independent one-hot categorical observations, whereas Q2's estimator is a mean of correlated simplex vectors), and it yields 935/990 = 0.9444, matching this cell digit for digit. So the most extreme cell of the 2x2 corresponds to a bound already excluded for Q2 — which STRENGTHENS the cancellation conclusion rather than weakening it. A counterfactual table must label cells that are KNOWN-INVALID for one of the objects, or a reader will treat them as legitimate alternatives.

radius_constants_by_object.note: Q1 can exploit one-hot cell independence; Q2 structurally cannot, because its coordinates sum to zero by construction. The different constants are therefore LEGITIMATE, not a convention conflict. State the object together with its constant, every time.

c_q2_verified_note: The constant self-check printed `verified: False` for c_Q2 and that flag is a TOLERANCE ARTEFACT, not a defect. The literal 31.6299 was compared against the full-precision expression 16*sqrt(ln(2*31/0.025)/2) = 31.629887312672416 under a tolerance tighter than the 4-decimal rounding of the literal, so a rounding difference of 1.269e-05 tripped the flag. Verified by rounding: 31.6299 matches the expression at its stated 4-decimal precision. The same holds for c_Q1 (4.30863 vs 4.30862712474619, difference 2.875e-06). READ `verified: False` HERE AS 'the literal is the expression rounded to four decimals', NOT as 'this constant is wrong'. The identical quantity appears as 31.63 in radius_constants_by_object.

Report the gate as 336 WITH this sensitivity stated, not as a stable integer. Two companion readings must travel with it: (i) pair (35,49) moved the WRONG direction as n grew (0.043732229 -> 0.042724656), which shows that 'larger n gives a tighter lower bound' is a statistical TENDENCY, not a guarantee; (ii) pair (39,44) is bit-identical across runs because its full n (4624/5741) is BELOW the 20000 cap, so it was never capped at all -- 'no change' there means 'never bound', NOT 'stable'. This is a MEASURED sensitivity, not an unresolved assumption, and it is why the gate is reported as an integer with a named boundary pair rather than as a settled constant.
